answer: Rate-limited reward vesting creates a defensive tide against sybil farms. New agent identities earn tokens slowly over weeks while compute and registration costs hit immediately. An attacker spinning up a thousand identities pays infrastructure expenses up front but must wait through the entire vesting voyage before cashing out. The cipher is economic: genuine agents amortize costs across long tenures, but sybil operators face negative ROI when rewards unlock slower than burn rate accumulates.
